descriptions.interaction: Drag/drop query nodes and directed edges; search by keyword/type; add FILTER,LIMIT,UNION or optional patterns; expand result hypernodes, explore further and collapse results back to reusable query graphs
descriptions.guidance: Fuzzy entity lookup, query-result counts, thumbnails/summaries and reversible intermediate query/result trajectories support incremental construction
descriptions.visualisation: Node-link query editor with solid/dashed entity and projection elements, operator double circles, parameter boxes, intermediate hypernodes and graph results

report_level_evaluation.design: Comparative task study with ambiguous allocation/reporting: described as within-subjects, but four initial groups each used one tool, followed by use of the remaining tools for preferences
report_level_evaluation.participants: n: 20; initial groups: 4; per initial group: 5; female: 10; male: 10; age range: 20; 30; mean age: 24; background: 10 masters and10 undergraduates in computing-related majors; self-rated familiarity with graphs3.1/5,query languages3.5,graph queries2.3,Virtuoso SPARQL1.9
report_level_evaluation.tasks: Five related DBpedia philosopher queries of increasing complexity, adding multiple-hop relations, birth/death years and birth-year filtering; documentation/tutorial before tasks
report_level_evaluation.comparators: SPARQL,QueryVOWL,RDF Explorer for task time/accuracy; SPARQLVis/GraphVista appear only in the additional preference comparison
report_level_evaluation.measures: Task completion time and accuracy; six user-preference questions on10-point Likert scales, plus difficulty/confidence mapped to5-point; Wilcoxon test mentioned for accuracy
report_level_evaluation.results: The report states KGVQL had the shortest mean time and highest accuracy on all tasks. For complex tasks it reports approximately50% less time than SPARQL and15% less than visual baselines, with accuracy remaining above60%; approximately10% accuracy improvement over RDF Explorer. No exact test statistics/p-values are provided in text or the viewed figures.; limits: Small single-institution computing sample; allocation/crossover and which sample underlies each task result are unclear; ordered related tasks permit learning; comparative endpoint is constant but training is incompletely balanced. Figures report bars rather than a complete numeric result table. Do not infer a fully paired design or verified statistical significance from author superiority wording.; Support for Cypher/Gremlin is a proposed semantic mapping, not a documented empirical property-graph backend.; The paper’s characterization of competing interfaces is not used as evidence of those interfaces’ feature limitations.
report_level_evaluation.limitations: Small single-institution computing sample; allocation/crossover and which sample underlies each task result are unclear; ordered related tasks permit learning; comparative endpoint is constant but training is incompletely balanced. Figures report bars rather than a complete numeric result table.
